title: improv·artist · mythic (Anselm Kiefer)
mutation_directive: improv artist: mythic via Anselm Kiefer

improv_extras.practice: ash, lead, straw; history as wound; vast leaden landscapes

v1.feedback: The Kiefer brief clearly drove the design — scorched stalks with drooping seed-heads, ground ash, falling embers, and a lead/burnt-sienna/gold palette all land. The stalks read as vertical forms within ~2s, which is good. To refine: the additive blending risks blowing out stalk clusters to white where particles overlap — switch to normal blending or multiply so dense areas darken into charcoal rather than glow; the falling ash is generic slow-drift and could sell 'aftermath' harder if particles started large and fractured/shrank as they fell; and consider a very slow camera dolly or subtle upward tilt to give the field the monumental Kiefer scale — right now the fixed mid-height camera flattens what should feel like a vast wounded landscape.

v2.feedback: The Kiefer channel lands well — scorched vertical stalks with drooping seed heads read as a burned wheat field within 2 seconds, and the charcoal/burnt-sienna/lead-grey/ash-gold palette is genuinely restrained and material-appropriate. The falling ash with fracture-shrink lifecycle is a nice touch that earns its compute. To push this further: the camera is static and slightly too far back, making the stalks feel small against the dark void — pull the camera closer (z~14) or add a very slow dolly so the leaden landscape feels vast rather than distant. The ground plane reads as empty blackness; a subtle stippled ground-ash layer with slight elevation variation would sell the 'landscape' aspect Kiefer's work demands and fill the lower third of the frame.
